answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because sparrow only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, ripple is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any juniper approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
